questions.text:
The following functional dependencies hold true for the relational schema R{V,W,X,Y,Z}:
V [latex]\rightarrow[/latex]W
VW [latex]\rightarrow[/latex]X
Y[latex]\rightarrow[/latex] VX
Y [latex]\rightarrow[/latex]Z
Which of the following is irreducible equivalent for this set of functional dependencies ?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]VW\rightarrow X[/latex]: W is extra because V [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] W, so it becomes [latex]V\rightarrow X[/latex].
- [latex]Y\rightarrow VX[/latex] splits into [latex]Y\rightarrow V[/latex] and [latex]Y\rightarrow X[/latex]; the latter is redundant ([latex]Y\rightarrow V\rightarrow X[/latex]).

Minimal cover: [latex]V\rightarrow W,\ V\rightarrow X,\ Y\rightarrow V,\ Y\rightarrow Z[/latex]

Answer: Option 1

questions.text:
Consider the following grammar.

P[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]xQRS
Q[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]yz|z
R[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]w|[latex]\varepsilon[/latex]
S[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]y

What is FOLLOW (Q) ?
questions.solution:
In [latex]P\rightarrow xQRS[/latex], Q is followed by RS. FIRST(R) = {w, [latex]\varepsilon[/latex]}, so FOLLOW(Q) gets w, and since R can vanish, FIRST(S) = {y} too.

FOLLOW(Q) = {w, y}

Answer: {w, y}

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

Threads of the same process share the whole address space, including global variables and the heap. Only the stack and registers are private.

Answer: Both heap and global variables

questions.text:
Let X be a Gaussian random variable mean 0 and variance [latex]\sigma ^{2}[/latex]
. Let Y=max(X, 0) where max
(a,b) is the maximum of a and b. The median of Y is ____________.
questions.solution:
X is symmetric about 0, so P(X [latex]\le[/latex] 0) = 0.5. Y = max(X, 0) equals 0 whenever X [latex]\le[/latex] 0, so [latex]P(Y\le0)=0.5[/latex] and [latex]P(Y\ge0)=1[/latex]. The median of Y is 0.

Answer: 0

questions.text: Let T be a tree with 10 vertices. The sum of the degrees of all the vertices in T is _________.
questions.solution:
A tree with 10 vertices has 9 edges. Sum of degrees = 2 [latex]\times[/latex] edges = 18.

Answer: 18
